note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: Does a steam pressure-reducing valve between headers pass enough steam to drive a backpressure turbogenerator instead?

evidence.text: valve PCV-A reads "PCV-A PRV Steam HP HEADER station"; owning equipment unknown; no unit inferred; supplied source interpretation, not installed truth; Recorded qualifiers: {"tag": "PCV-A", "kind": "final_element", "unit": null, "source": "Fictional candidate station, not installed-state proof", "assigned_tag": true, "unplaced_reason": "Fictional explicitly unplaced station; no inventoried equipment owner"}; Assigned identifier; an operating tag has not been verified

data_requests.item: Steam flow through the station over a year
where: only a valve (PCV-A) is drawn on this line, with no flow measurement; flow needs a meter or a calibrated valve curve

questions.decision_rule: Consider a backpressure turbogenerator only if the station passes a constant flow of at least 3,000 lb/hr with a pressure drop of at least 100 psi (S6's condition); otherwise close this screening investigation.

typical_benefit.wording: Consider when a PRV has "constant steam flows of at least 3,000 pounds per hour (lb/hr), and when the steam pressure drop is at least 100 psi." Installation costs "typically average 75% of equipment costs".
source_titles: S6: Steam Tip #20, Replace Pressure-Reducing Valves with Backpressure Turbogenerators (DOE/GO-102012-3409)

questions.limits: S6 also quotes cost per kW figures; they are deliberately not repeated here. No IAC code maps to turbines (2.2134 covers PRV-station leaks).
